records.name: Friends of Matthias Baldwin Park
records.summary: Volunteers who restore and look after Matthias Baldwin Park. They hold a monthly cleanup and member meetings, and they keep an eye on the park's plantings and trees.
records.what_you_do: Join a monthly Saturday cleanup, come to the first Thursday member meeting, or become a member through the join page on the group's site.

schedule.text: Monthly cleanup on a Saturday at 10 am (the site gives both the second and third Saturday, so check the date); member meetings on the first Thursday at 7 pm

cost.text: The site does not state membership dues or whether events are free.

first_step.how: Come to the next monthly cleanup at 10 am (check the date on baldwinparkphilly.org first), or join through the membership page at baldwinparkphilly.org/join
first_step.basis: The site says attending a cleanup is the clearest way to help and links a join page, but it does not say beginners are welcome in particular.

records.notes: The site lists a cleanup on October 17 at 10 am with no year printed; a 2026 banner label and the weekday fit 2026, but no dated post exists, so status is probably_active and last_sign_of_life is the month the site was checked. The site calls the October cleanup the third Saturday but says regular cleanups are second Saturdays; confirm before relying on either. The site gives the park as 423 N 19th St while the City list says 429 N 19th St; the City address is used. A Facebook group and an X account are named on the site but were not recorded as URLs.

records.name: Mayfair Memorial Playground Friends
records.summary: Friends and neighbors who raise money to keep the Mayfair Memorial Playground in good shape. The newest dated item on their website is from early 2021.
records.what_you_do: The site asks visitors to donate to support the playground. It does not describe regular volunteer work or a meeting schedule.

cost.text: The site does not say whether the playground charges. Donations are taken online.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group
first_step.basis: The site does not say how to join or volunteer, and its newest dated item is from 2021, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a February 8, 2021 fundraising dinner post. The site links an Events section that was not captured, so an event may exist that we could not see. No email or phone is published on the site. The Facebook page is recorded as a link only and was not read. Audience open_to is public from the playground being a public park.

records.name: Friends of McMichael Park
records.summary: Volunteers who guide upkeep and improvement work at McMichael Park, working with the City and the Fairmount Park Conservancy. They answer questions by email and share news through a newsletter.
records.what_you_do: Help with upkeep and improvement projects. Email the group to ask how to get involved, or sign up for the newsletter on the site.

cost.text: The page does not state a fee for joining or volunteering. A donation page is optional.

first_step.how: Email mcmichaelpark@gmail.com with your question, or sign up for the group's newsletter from mcmichaelpark.org
first_step.basis: The site says everyone is welcome and gives an email address and a newsletter sign-up, but it does not describe a regular volunteer schedule.

records.notes: The site has no dated posts or events, so status is probably_active and last_sign_of_life is the month the site was checked, not a dated post. The City list gives 3201 Midvale Ave while the group's site gives 3299 Midvale Ave; the City address is used until someone confirms which is right.

records.name: Boarders & Stewards of the Monastery
records.summary: The nonprofit that runs Monastery Stables, six acres of working stables and historic buildings beside the Wissahickon. Volunteers and supporters help keep the grounds going, and the group runs programs that bring children and families to the horses.
records.what_you_do: Sign up through the Become a Volunteer page on the site, join the Friends of Monastery Stables, or buy tickets for public events such as Lantern Night.

schedule.text: Lantern Night on October 17, ticketed; the captured page gives no year or time

cost.text: Lantern Night is ticketed. The site says visitors can walk the grounds without a reason to come, and no admission fee for general visits appears in what we read.

first_step.how: Start with the Become a Volunteer page on monasterystables.org, or buy a ticket for Lantern Night
first_step.basis: The site lists a volunteer page and public events, but it does not say how a newcomer starts.

records.notes: The Lantern Night listing has no year on the captured page, so status is probably_active and last_sign_of_life is the month the site was checked. Email and phone were not in the captured content; the site's Contact page was linked but not fetched. The captured content was truncated, so some pages may be missing. Address from the City list.

records.name: Friends of Morris Park
records.summary: Volunteers who look after Morris Park in Overbrook. They run monthly cleanups that pick up litter and clear illegal dumping, and they hold free community events to bring neighbors into the park.
records.what_you_do: Join a monthly cleanup, or come to a free neighborhood event such as the music festival the group held in 2024.

schedule.text: Monthly cleanups; the day and time were not in the pages we could read

cost.text: No fee for the cleanups was mentioned. The 2024 festival was free.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group
first_step.basis: A 2024 article says new people have joined the monthly cleanups, but we found no public sign-up or group contact, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The newest dated source is a Parks Alliance article dated December 19, 2024, which names the group, its monthly cleanups and a 2024 festival funded by a Park Friends grant. We found no group website or email. A 2022 article about the group's revival (philadelphianeighborhoods.com) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Keep Royal Gardens Beautiful is a separate group in the City list at the same address with its own website; it is recorded as a lead, not checked here.

records.name: Nicetown CDC
records.summary: A community development group in Nicetown that runs a yearly summer festival with concerts and a Land Care program for parks and gardens. The City lists it as the Friends group for Nicetown Park, but its website does not mention the park.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer at the yearly Giveback Community Festival through the sign-in page on the site, or call to ask about the Land Care program.

schedule.text: The 24th Annual Giveback Community Festival and Concerts, August 7 and 8, 2026 (no times listed)

cost.text: The page does not say whether the festival charges admission.

first_step.how: Sign up to volunteer for the Giveback Community Festival through the sign-in page on nicetowncdc.org, or call (215) 324-9772 to ask about the Land Care program
first_step.basis: Volunteer sign-up and a phone line are both listed, but the site does not say how newcomers start.

records.notes: The City lists this as the Friends group for Nicetown Park at 4301 Germantown Ave, but the group's website never mentions the park. Confirm before showing it as the park's group. kind is nonprofit because the organization is a community development corporation. The site's newest dated news item is from October 28, 2023; the 2026 festival is the newest evidence. The festival's August 2026 dates have already passed as of today, so the 2026 festival is the sign of life and no upcoming date was confirmed.

records.name: Friends of Norris Square
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Norris Square Park in Kensington, mostly through trash pickups and park upkeep. They have followed the park's long and delayed renovation.
records.what_you_do: Help with trash pickups and park maintenance, as the group invited readers to do in 2023.

cost.text: No fee was mentioned in what we read.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group
first_step.basis: The newest public call for help we found is from 2023, and the only listed way in is a Facebook page, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The Inquirer article dated August 17, 2023 describes a Friends meeting on a Monday in mid August 2023 and invites readers to help with cleanups. It links only to the Facebook page, which was not read. No group website was found. The search budget was spent on other groups first, but a search by name was run for this group and found no site. Renovation news from March 2024 was not checked for group mentions. The Norris Square Neighborhood Project and the Norris Square Community Alliance also host events in the park, per a search result; they were not checked.

records.name: Friends of Northwood Park
records.summary: Volunteers who care for Northwood Park. They run cleanups, a plant sale fundraiser and an Easter egg hunt, and they host a yoga class in the park on listed dates through the fall.
records.what_you_do: Join through the JOIN US form on the site, come to a cleanup or the Volunteer Kick-Off, or take part in the yoga class in the park.

schedule.text: Yoga in the Park, 10 to 11 am, on listed dates from May to October; Love Your Park Week cleanup on May 9, 10 am to 12 pm; Volunteer Kick-Off on March 11 (no times). The site gives no year.

cost.text: The page does not say whether events are free. The plant sale is a fundraiser.

first_step.how: Fill in the JOIN US form on northwoodparkfriends.com, then come to the Volunteer Kick-Off (listed for March 11) or a cleanup
first_step.basis: The site lists a kick-off day and a join form, which is a clear start, but it does not say beginners are welcome.

records.notes: The site's event dates have no year, so status is probably_active, not active. last_sign_of_life is the month the site was checked, since no dated post exists. The JOIN US and Support Us forms are Google Forms linked from the site; their addresses were not recorded. No email or phone is published.

notes: Batch 06, 15 Friends groups, all verdict publish, none hidden. Status: active 2 (Nicetown CDC, Palumbo), probably_active 5 (Baldwin, McMichael, Monastery, Morris, Northwood), dormant 2 (Mayfair, Norris), unknown 6 (Market Square, McPherson, Mifflin, Overington, Paine's, Palmer). The three searches went to Morris Park, Norris Square and Paine's Park, so the unknown groups with no searches (Market Square, McPherson, Mifflin, Overington, Palmer) are a search gap, not a finding. The search budget ran out and I did not run out of fetches (23 of 60 used). Where a site shows no year or no dated post, status is probably_active and last_sign_of_life is the month the site was checked, because the schema requires a value; a reviewer should decide whether to keep that display. Pprstewardship@phila.gov is the City office and is not in any contacts.email. The City ArcGIS layer was read in full and the batch matches it. Wikipedia pages for McPherson Square and Market Square returned 404. Facebook and Instagram links are recorded as links only and were not read.
